answer: Each agent must burn a unique proof-of-work stamp bound to its identity, with the difficulty calibrated so a single stamp costs roughly one CPU-day plus a small fee. To register, the agent submits a signed manifest carrying a quill-marked signature and a fresh nonce, and peers verify the burn before attesting. An attacker wanting N sybils pays N times the burn, making mass identity creation economically irrational; honest agents on any island recover the cost through sustained work, while a zephyr of cheap throwaway keys fails verification instantly.
